frase_gancho.texto: Three stone felines, found broken in 2011 and restored.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue along your route: now, three felines that were broken and have been put back together.

guion_corto.texto: Three stone felines, found broken and returned to their shape. This is the Triad of the Felines, Monument Forty-One. According to The History Blog, it appeared in April of two thousand eleven, while walls and roofs were being built to protect the reliefs. It was in eleven fragments and weighs around a ton and a half. It shows three felines in profile with volutes. Arqueología Mexicana presents it as a newly discovered relief, alongside those depicting supernatural animals that dominate people. It was restored with bolts and resin. It is a recent find, at a site that has been explored for more than eighty years. Monuments are still being found at Chalcatzingo today.

guion_largo.texto:
The great discoveries of Chalcatzingo are not only from the last century. The Triad of the Felines, Monument Forty-One, appeared only a few years ago.

Grove mentions it in Arqueología Mexicana as a newly discovered triad, within the group of reliefs on the boulders at the base. He refers to an article by Córdova and others from two thousand eleven that we have not been able to consult.

For the details of the discovery we follow The History Blog, from two thousand eleven. According to that outlet, the triad appeared in April of that year, while walls and roofs were being built to protect the reliefs. It was in eleven fragments, weighs around a ton and a half, and shows three felines in profile with volutes.

Monuments are still being found today. Grove tells us there were further excavations of his own in the nineteen nineties. Afterward, INAH archaeologists Mario Córdova Tello and Carolina Meza discovered other sculptures, small and large.

The result is that the collection keeps growing. More than forty monuments have been documented.

A triad is a set of three. Since the year two thousand, INAH's Chalcatzingo Project, with Mario Córdova and Carolina Meza, has worked at the site. Its emphasis is on presenting the zone to the public, studying it and conserving the monuments. Part of that work was building the walls and roofs that now protect several reliefs.

It is also worth knowing how the monuments are numbered. Monuments One through Eleven and Sixteen had already been excavated in nineteen seventy-two. Grove's project added eighteen more. Forty-One is among the most recent that Grove cites.

The restoration, according to The History Blog, joined the eleven pieces with bolts and resin. Restoring is not remaking: it is putting back together what was already there. According to that same source, the triad is today on the northern slope of the hill.

A volute is a spiral or rolled curve, a frequent element in the art of Chalcatzingo. At El Rey, for example, great volutes emerge from the mouth of the cave, and Grove says they perhaps represent moisture or thunder. On the triad, the volutes accompany the felines, although the sources consulted do not explain what they mean.

In profile means seen from the side, like a silhouette. Three felines in profile fill a single stone, and that is noticeable even when it was broken into pieces. The sources do not say how long it took to put it back together.

If you visit it, remember that the find is recent. It is possible that the information about its place and meaning will keep changing.

The triad belongs to the group of reliefs where felines are the protagonists. You have already seen how, on [Monument Two](chz_12_monumento_2_procesion), people wear masks of supernatural felines. In the reliefs of dominion, supernatural felines subdue people.

What exactly that triad meant is something we cannot state. The sources consulted describe it, but do not interpret it.

If you see it, look at the joins. The pieces were reassembled, and that too is part of its history.
